children: Malaysia's near-term export growth momentum remains favorable, say Kenanga economists in a note. Demand for electrical and electronics product exports is expected to be sustained, driven by AI-related technology investment and new product launches, but growth is expected to slow in 2H as favorable base effects fade, they say. There are also risks from renewed U.S. trade policy uncertainty, weaker global growth amid higher energy prices, geopolitical tensions and a potential slowdown in electronics demand after the AI investment cycle, they reckon. Kenanga raises its Malaysia's export growth forecast for 2026 to 28.5% from 19.0% projected earlier, given strong year-to-date growth and strength in external demand through 3Q. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
